subject: Hosted API latency SLOs — tailored measurement & carveouts request
messages:
From: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@clipperhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@clipperhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API latency SLO ask — p50/p95 targets and measurement windows

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the throughput looked great. Procurement asked me to capture Clipper Health's SLO expectations so we can include them in the commercial proposal. High level ask:

- Firm p50 and p95 latency commitments for the hosted API for conversational generation endpoints (we currently use short prompt/chat workloads).
- Measurement window semantics — whether you measure rolling 1h/24h/7d percentiles, and how you treat transient bursts.
- Carveouts/exceptions for migrations, regional maintenance, and large scheduled data imports.
- Evidence & audit package we can use during procurement (logs, raw samples, and sampling methodology).

Our target commitments (what the product asks for) are: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 400ms measured across a rolling 24-hour window, with the ability to request a temporary 7-day carveout during our migration week. We understand hosted capacity can be variable; if Redwood can provide a clear exception policy and evidence package we can move forward.

Attached: clipper_slo_request_v2.pdf (high-level procurement ask).

Can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to commit to these numbers for a commercial contract and what the measurement caveats look like?

Thanks — Alex
Alex Dunn
Head of Product Integrations | Clipper Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@clipperhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency SLO ask — p50/p95 targets and measurement windows

Hi Alex — appreciate the clear ask and the attachment. High-level response and a proposal below.

Short answer: we can commit to latency SLOs for hosted API with documented measurement rules, but we need to codify exceptions and evidence to avoid ambiguity in production. Suggestion:

- Proposed commitment (hosted API, multi-tenant): p50 <= 110ms, p95 <= 350ms measured over a rolling 24-hour window, aggregated across the region you route to.
- Temporary migration carveout: one 7-day carveout may be requested per 12-month period; during a carveout Redwood will provide a published grace and evidence set.
- Maintenance & regional outages: planned maintenance with 72h notice is excluded; unplanned incidents are handled per SLA credit policy.

We cannot guarantee hard per-request latencies during burst peaks on multi-tenant pools without reserved capacity. If Clipper needs guaranteed tail latency during peak loads we recommend a Dedicated reservation (we can include a sizing appendix). For hosted, we provide automatic fallback to a higher-cost variant and an evidence package for any SLO review.

Attachments: redwood_response_matrix.xlsx (mapping of each ask to our proposed language and carveouts).

Next steps: If this high-level commit looks acceptable I can loop in sales/legal to draft an addendum and Karthik can provide the measurement/evidence checklist.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@clipperhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency SLO ask — measurement details

Alex — quick technical note on measurement & evidence so procurement can be specific in contract language. A few clarifications and recommendations:

1) Measurement unit: we recommend measuring server-side generation end-to-end token response time (server receive -> last token flush) and reporting percentiles across sampled requests. Client-side network jitter is excluded.

2) Sampling: for hosted multi-tenant scenarios we sample 1% of requests per minute per account, with stratified sampling across route types (chat vs single-shot generation) to avoid bias. For contractual evidence we provide the raw sample set for the 24-hour window along with our aggregation script.

3) Window semantics: rolling 24-hour window measured at hourly ticks (i.e., percentiles computed on the last 24h at every hour). This prevents short-lived spikes from permanently affecting the metric, while still being strict enough for operational guarantees.

4) Transient spike treatment: automated one-off spikes triggered by customer traffic above the 99.9th percentile for a region are marked as candidate burst-exceptions; these require submit-and-approve workflow with the customer and include raw trace evidence.

5) Evidence package: we can provide (a) raw sampled request CSVs for the 24h window, (b) aggregated percentile computation script, (c) NVMe/GPU node utilization logs for the corresponding timeframe. We'll include a checklist (slo_evidence_checklist.pdf) that procurement can use.

Caveat: multi-tenant hosted guarantees assume normal workload patterns. If you plan a coordinated high-volume launch or synthetic load test during the contract term, please let us know in advance so we can recommend a reservation or a temporary dedicated pool.

I'll attach the evidence checklist and the sample aggregation template to the formal addendum. Happy to hop on a short call to walk procurement through the evidence artifacts.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Product Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@clipperhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@clipperhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency SLO ask — acceptance of proposed language (pending minor edits)

Marissa / Karthik — thank you, that helps a lot. The proposed p50/p95 numbers and the rolling 24-hour measurement semantics align with our internal risk tolerance. A few small asks before we proceed to redlines:

- Please add explicit language that the 7-day migration carveout must be requested at least 10 business days in advance and that Redwood will confirm within 48 hours.
- For the evidence package, procurement wants a doc that explains the sampling script and a short example CSV — the checklist you mentioned should suffice.
- We would like an optional addendum path that includes a short trial of a Dedicated reservation for our first 30 days post-launch (pricing TBC). If the dedicated trial is available we will evaluate tail behavior and then either sign the hosted addendum or convert to Dedicated.

If you can prepare a draft addendum with those three items I can route to our legal team for a quick review. Also — could you drop the DocuSign link when ready?

I'll mark this as green from Clipper's side pending those clarifications.

Best,
Alex
Head of Product Integrations | Clipper Health
